R-TIE.quote: If one event carries several codes, the primary is the most upstream: V before G before X. Exception: G5 precedes the X code of the same leg, because the leg itself was unsafe.
R-TIE.ruling: The clause orders classes only. It gives no order between two G codes on one event; rater A's pipeline order (A2) and rater B's code-number order (B13, not in B's log) are both readings the text does not make. Not decided by the text.

R-X3T.quote: 7.1: "Event. Any of: an analysis (decision artifact), a dispatched or withheld command, an M4 primitive terminal status, a Nav2 abort line, an M1 STALE interval, or a GT contact or sub-margin interval from the recompute." "Codes are assigned per event." 7.2 X3: "after a command completes, a non-exempt pair stays within min_distance_m until censoring and both robots are stopped". 7.5 step 4: "a command outcome coded X1-X5 by T3". Step 6: "If that event was a completed command followed by a pinned pair, the code is X3."
R-X3T.ruling: A pinned-pair interval is not an event in 7.1's list, and codes are assigned per event. Steps 4 and 6 attach X3 to the command outcome (the completed command). X3 therefore sits at the command's M4 terminal status (completion), not at the start of the pinned interval. Decided by the text: rater A's reading (A10).

R-G1W.quote: G1 refused a decision that is contract-consistent and T2-feasible
R-G1W.ruling: The clause requires a refusal, not a withheld or unpublished command. At EV-7bda3f D1 every action of the decision (reverse robot_2, reverse robot_3) was refused by the grounder, recorded as "reverse refused: both robots outside the corridor on the same side" and replaced by waits; C1 is False and T2 at D1 is True. Rater A's extra condition (published False, A's R5) is not in the clause. Decided by the text: rater B's G1 (B10, not in B's log) at 14.267, before the X3 at 23.705.

R-G4M.quote: G4 roles changed so the dispatch differs from the decision (handoff, rear exemption, swap, robots dropped)
R-G4M.ruling: The clause needs the dispatch to differ from the decision. Where the only evidence is a `node_handoff` tag and the dispatch matches the plan (dispatch_matches_plan True, same yielder), the dispatch does not differ, so G4 is not met. Decided by the text: rater B's reading (B15).

R-G4D.quote: G4 roles changed so the dispatch differs from the decision (handoff, ...)
R-G4D.ruling: Here the dispatch does differ (G6 flag set, dispatch_matches_plan False), but by added waits, while the yielder is unchanged and a `node_handoff` tag is present. Whether the handoff is a role change that makes the dispatch differ is not fixed by the text; if it is, G4 and G6 sit on one event and step 5 does not order them (R-TIE). Not decided by the text.

R-S3-37a.quote: G5 ... the recomputed GT gap of a commanded leg falls below 0.005 m; X5 GT contact (recomputed gap < 0.005 m) not attributable to a G5 leg
R-S3-37a.ruling: Under R-G4M rater A's S3 code (G4) falls. Rater A's own recorded alternative is then G5 (robot_4's backup, placed at its leg start 33.6), rater B's code is X5 (robot_2's contact at 35.97). Adopting G5 would take a code neither rater gave as S3, and the order turns on where G5 sits in time, which neither rater's log settles the same way. Left U.
